issues.description: The solution implementation of assembleBookstore introduces a parameter (assembleBookstore(check: Bool)) while the problem statement and the template expect a parameterless function assembleBookstore() -> Bookstore. Additionally, the solution's main() calls assembleBookstore() with no arguments, which conflicts with the parameterized signature. This mismatch in method parameters will confuse students and prevent the code from compiling as-is.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the assembleBookstore function signature consistent with the problem statement and template by removing the unexpected parameter. Change the solution implementation signature to: private static func assembleBookstore() -> Bookstore { ... } so that calls to assembleBookstore() without arguments compile and match the specification.

issues.description: The helper function assembleBookstore is referenced in the problem statement and the template as a no-argument method (assembleBookstore() -> Bookstore), but the solution defines it with a parameter (assembleBookstore(check: Bool) -> Bookstore). This signature mismatch (extra parameter name) creates a mapping and compilation confusion for students: the template/comment suggests implementing a no-arg function, the solution's implementation uses a different signature, and Client.main() in the solution calls assembleBookstore() with no arguments — an inconsistency that will confuse students about the expected function signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the function signature across all artifacts. Change the solution implementation to the no-argument signature expected by the template and problem: private static func assembleBookstore() -> Bookstore { ... } and ensure Client.main() calls assembleBookstore() accordingly (or, if a parameter is required for pedagogical reasons, update the problem statement and template to declare the same parameter and its purpose).
